comments.author: @LifewaysTravel
comments.text: Tutuila is one of those places most people have never heard of, yet its story is incredible. 🌊 With the island slowly sinking, would you choose to stay and protect your family's homeland or leave for a safer future? We'd love to hear your thoughts! Thanks for watching and being part of this journey! ❤

replies.author: @LifewaysTravel
replies.text: @TiaoaliiLutu Not quite my imagination 😄 NASA actually measured Tutuila sinking by an average of 6-9 mm per year between 2015 and 2022, following the 2009 earthquake. It's called land subsidence. That doesn't mean the entire island is about to disappear, but it does increase the risk of coastal flooding. Here's the NASA study if you're curious: https://www.nasa.gov/centers-and-facilities/goddard/nasa-researchers-measure-sinking-land-in-american-samoa/

comments.author: @PeterLepou
comments.text: I swear something about this video feels so off. First, you said that 48,000 people here are struggling to make a living. Where exactly are you getting your information? Sikeeee! American Samoa is one of the least commercialized and most culturally grounded U.S. territories. Stop creating documentaries that paint our island in such a negative light just to get views. Your entire documentary is AI-generated, and the information you're presenting is misleading and inaccurate. If you're going to talk about our island, at least do your research and get your facts straight. Nice try, though!

replies.author: @LifewaysTravel
replies.text: I can understand why that wording bothered you. The 48,000 figure refers to the island's approximate population, not the number of people struggling financially. We should have made that distinction clearer. Also, there,s a real team behind the research, writing, and editing of our documentaries. I'd genuinely like to hear more from you, though. What do you think we got most wrong about life in American Samoa? 🇦🇸
